question: How is the knowable reality distinguished from thought while ruling the time of knowing?
premises: The reality is not mere thought
It is to be known and understood
It is described as ruling the time of what is to be known
inference: The knowable reality transcends thought and governs the occasion of knowing.
uncertainties: The compound jñātavya-kāla-śāsanaḥ is interpretively dense.
plain_english: It is not thought; rather, it is to be known, the ruler of the time of what is to be known.
